components.title: Sterling workbench
components.description: The Sterling workbench image that a hosted site runs for each person.

control-implementations.description: What the Sterling workbench's unit tests, in the workbench package's report, show about its hosted session.

implemented-requirements.description: Secrets an extension saves go to the person's own OpenBao path, never to memory.

statements.description: In a hosted session the workbench rebinds Theia's key store, through which its extensions keep their secrets, to a store that writes, reads, lists and deletes them under the person's own OpenBao KV path (kv/data/users/<entity id>/<service>/<account>) with the session's own OpenBao token. With no active session every call is refused and OpenBao is not called, and an OpenBao refusal or silence becomes a plain sentence that holds no secret, token or entity id. On a single computer the store is the system keyring; when the keyring cannot load, saving fails, and Theia's in-memory store is never used.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's OpenBao with the per-person KV policy and decides which secrets people may keep there.
